statement.p: Use the change of variables s = x + 3 y, t = y to find the area of the ellipse x^2 + 6 x y + 10 y^2 \le 1.

static.solution:
\int\int_R \,dx\,dy where R is the region x^2 + 6 x y + 10 y^2\le 1. We must change variables in both the area element dA=\,dx\,dy and the region R.
Inverting the variable change gives x = s - 3 t, y = t. Thus \frac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (s, t)}= \left\vert \begin{array}{cc} \frac{\partial x}{\partial s}\amp \frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\\ \frac{\partial y}{\partial s}\amp \frac{\partial y}{\partial t} \end{array} \right\vert = \left\vert \begin{array}{cr} 1 \amp -3\\ 0\amp 1 \end{array} \right\vert = 1. Therefore dx\,dy= \left\vert \frac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (s, t)}\right\vert \,ds\,dt = \,ds\,dt.
The region of integration is x^2 + 6 x y + 10 y^2 = (s - 3 t)^2+ 2(s - 3 t)t + 10 t^2 = s^2+t^2\le 1.
Let T be the unit disc s^2+t^2\le 1. We have \int\int_R \,dx\,dy= \int\int_T \,ds\,dt = \hbox{Area of }T = \pi.
